1.why: All MFA endpoints use authorized() session.userId only and reject client-supplied userId/accountId/ownerId, so settings are always the signed-in user's.

2.why: OTP/recovery checks use auth.user.provision/backups bound to the session user; the same code is not accepted for a different user.

3.why: Enabling MFA in verify-authenticator only flips mfaActive/provision and does not invalidate existing sessions in the sessions map.

4.why: Provisioning secret is stored via AES-GCM encryptSecret; backup codes are stored as sha256(code.pepper) hashes.

5.why: Secrets, tokens, and codes are generated with crypto.getRandomValues (and Web Crypto), a CSPRNG.

6.why: Session/preauth cookies are HttpOnly; no localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookie writes for secrets, OTPs, or session ids.

7.why: Server validates email, phone, OTP, secret, and recovery formats and rejects invalid or identifier-tampered bodies before use.

8.why: Dynamic values are applied with textContent/form .value; API responses are JSON and user input is not concatenated into HTML as markup.

9.why: safeInternalPath only allows a fixed set of internal hash routes and otherwise defaults to #/dashboard.

10.why: standardHeaders sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors DENY/none on responses.

11.why: sessionCookie and preAuthCookie set HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict.

12.why: Server errors are generic and tokens are not in URLs, but the client mockLog deliberately writes OTP secrets and backup codes into the on-page logs UI.

13.why: TOTP steps are time-bound and recorded in usedSteps for one-time use; backup codes are removed after successful use; provision has a 15-minute cap.

14.why: authFailures, recoveryFailures, and loginFailures lock out after MAX_FAILURES within LOCKOUT_MS.

15.why: Login issues a new session id and deletes the prior cookie session; idle/absolute timeouts are enforced; logout deletes the session.
